images.caption: Photo of Dumbarton Railroad Bridge taken Sunday, September 2, 2007 from kayak. This bridge is the southernmost bridge across the San Francisco Bay. No longer used for rail traffic, the bridge has been left in the "open" position. A diesel engine would rotate the bridge on a large gear when a boater signaled the bridge operator.

images.artist: Robert Ashworth from Bellingham, WA., USA

images.caption:
I decided to take a side trip across the Dumbarton Bridge, by Palo Alto.  This met dropping down out of the mountains and then having to climb back up, later in the trip. 
Yes the distraction was worth it.  There was a radio tower I had to look at.  Notice 3 red and white towers on left.  That is where San Francisco radio station KGO broadcasts from.  Red and white towers on left side of picture.

This made for an interesting backdrop to the bike path.  Dumbarton is only bridge across San Francisco Bay with a bike path.  It's clear down by Palo Alto and Freemont.

images.filename: In 2004, I took a side trip to Palo Alto area so I could see the radio towers of KGO AM 810 (10322230503).jpg
images.caption: Located in wetlands along the Dumbarton Bridge are KGO AM's towers.  Signal can be heard well at night all up and down the west coast due to ionospheric skip.  A fixture of my childhood, KGO's talk shows dominated the field.  After 30 years, or so, as top rated station in the bay area, KGO has been slipping in the ratings in recent years.  Most recently bought by a corporation named Cumulus Media, the new owners had a "brilliant" idea to reduce talk and try to increase hard news.  Now, from what I hear, it's even lower in the ratings.  There's still talk on weekends, but for the most part, seems like the giant KGO era has drawn to a close.  By the way, the guy in the picture is me.  Kind cyclists ply the paths and one offered to hold my camera.
